title: Design: the Sales Type column on Sales By Representative looks as designed
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Scenario: Today has a split work order, a work order with one person on both sides and a part sale, and you compare the Sales Type column with the design.
  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Two active staff members at {Location-A} have their "Sales Representative" switch on: {Sales-rep-A} and {Sales-rep-B}.
    For example: {Sales-rep-A} is ZZAUTOTEST Ann Able and {Sales-rep-B} is ZZAUTOTEST Ben Able.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has no sales representative.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST SSR Fleet.
  • Today has one invoiced split work order (Labor {Sales-rep-A}, Parts {Sales-rep-B}), one invoiced work order with {Sales-rep-A} on both sides and one invoiced part sale with no shop supplies.
  • The browser window is 1440 px wide with the zoom at 100%, and the design pictures "sbr-08-a4-columns-off.png" (board 4.8), "sbr-09-a4-columns-on.png" (board 4.9) and "sbr-10-a4-sbr-expanded-type.png" (board 4.10) attached to this case are open beside it at 100% (actual size). Names, numbers and dates in the pictures are sample data.
  • Starting screen: Reports > Sales By Representative is open for today in that browser window, with the Sales Type column off.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Open the column selector and compare with the picture of board 4.8.
  2. Turn Sales Type on and compare with the picture of board 4.9.
  3. Expand {Sales-rep-A}.
  4. Expand {Sales-rep-B} and compare with the picture of board 4.10.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: "Sales Type" is the first entry, off by default.
  • Step 2: switching it on adds the column right after Status (and before Location when the Location column shows).
  • Step 3: {Sales-rep-A}'s invoice rows show.
  • Step 4: the Sales Type column reads "Labor", "Parts", "Part Sales" and "Labor, Parts"; columns line up as in the picture and nothing overlaps.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 11 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10890, story SV-11269 (Story 5, Credit each side on the invoice and in Sales By Representative)

  • S5-R10: “When one person, or Unassigned, holds both the Labor and the Parts side of a work order and the Sales Type filter includes both, the two show as one row whose Sales Type reads "Labor, Parts" and whose figures are the sum of both sides.”
  • S5-R19: “An invoice row carries a "Sales Type" column, after Status and before Location (Status, Sales Type, Location), reading "Labor", "Parts", "Part Sales" or "Labor, Parts".”
  • S5-R20: “The Sales Type column is offered in the report's column selector, first in its list.”
  • S5-R21: “The Sales Type column is off by default on screen, for every user.”

From: Chris Ward's answers to the Splitting Sales Representatives question sheet (answers 1 to 38, 19 Oct 2026; answers 39 and 40, 21 Oct 2026), read 22 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward's answer 24: “24. (a) as the feature spec: a dash on screen and in the PDF, an empty cell in the CSV. The 0.0 rule still applies to an invoice with one person on both sides.”
  • Chris Ward's answer 25: “25. (a) A dash when the part sale has no shop supplies; $0.00 only when it has a shop supplies line that totals $0.00. The design's $0.00 is a sample-data mistake.”
  • Chris Ward's answer 26: “26. (a) Status, Sales Type, Location.”
  • Chris Ward's answer 36: “36. (b) Acceptable as shown, same as today's report.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Claude design canvas "Splitting Sales Representatives" (https://claude.ai/artifact/8MHqwyffAYtqZ6EccS5RUm), export read 19 Oct 2026, boards 4.8 The column picker; 4.9 Sales Type switched on; 4.10 Expanded with Sales Type (the attached pictures are these boards).

Where the design and the PRD differ: The picture of board 4.10 shows $0.00 under Shop Supplies on the Parts row and on the part sales; Chris Ward ruled on 19 Oct 2026 for the PRD's dash, and said the design's $0.00 on the part sales is a sample-data mistake (answers 24 and 25, quoted above), so the $0.00 in the picture is not what to expect. The "Column Selection" tooltip covering the Sales Type switch (board 4.8) is acceptable as today (answer 36, quoted above).

Design pictures attached to this case: sbr-08-a4-columns-off.png, sbr-09-a4-columns-on.png, sbr-10-a4-sbr-expanded-type.png.

  • Design — board 4.10 title: “4.10 Expanded with Sales Type”
